This outranks recovery and partial-coverage gaps because unimported functions represent silent routing rot: the routing layer can degrade or break without any test catching it, severing the conjecture-criticism dispatch pathway.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If these functions are confirmed to be dead code with no live callers in production, the test is unnecessary and this drops to the bottom.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the functions are exercised transitively by integration tests that would fail if they were deleted, a dedicated smoke test is redundant.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The cheapest test is a simple import-and-invoke smoke test: it calls resolve_conjecture_route with a minimal valid input and compile_criticism_assignments with a minimal valid assignment, asserting they return well-formed outputs without raising. If the functions are deleted or broken, the import or invocation fails. The blast radius is moderate-to-high: routing is the connective tissue of the harness; if it rots, requests are misrouted or dropped, but the append-only record itself remains intact (unlike Priorities 1 and 2). This is prioritized below security bypass because routing rot is a functional degradation, not a policy violation.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
